description.narrative: African women realise their rights as guaranteed in the African Women's Protocol
Stöd till en koalition av NGOs som arbetar för implementering av Maputo-protokollet om kvinnors rättigheter.
Support to a coalition of NGOs to achieve increased implementation of the Maputo protocol on women's rights.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative: The project has acheived the following results. These are;- . Contributed to the increased capacities of 198 women’s rights organization (WROs) to engage and advocate for legal reforms and domestication and implementation of the African Women’s Rights Protocol. . Contributed to the passing of three model laws informed by the Maputo Protocol: The Sexual Reproductive Health Act 2016 in Rwanda that lead to their President pardoning of 59 girls who were wrongly convicted of procuring abortion; The Gender Equal Opportunity Law in Nigeria and the passing of The Violence Against Persons Prohibition Act in Nigeria thus strengthening their legislative and legal framework on women’s rights.. Established and expanded existing coalitions that have been instrumental in effective advocacy at national and regional levels for enactment and implementation of model legislation and the Protocol. At the regional level the project has leveraged the efficacy of coalition work especially through Solidarity for African Women’s Rights Coalition (SOAWR) to add pressure on state parties to domesticate and implement the Protocol as was the case of Nigeria where SOAWR mounted pressure to the former President of Nigeria that saw the passing Violence Against People’s Prosecution Act in 2015.. Significant efforts have been made at regional level with our partner SOAWR making inroads in working with the African Union and its organs in pushing for state accountability. . They have provided technical support to AU in guiding states on implementation of normative standards /the African Women’s protocol through drafting and adoption of general comments on SRHR and one on ending child marriages in Africa.
